function.name: forget

function.name: get_ha_entities
function.description: Look up Home Assistant devices by domain and optionally by area or floor. Call this BEFORE control_device or get_device_status to find entity IDs. Example: user says 'turn on kitchen lights' → call get_ha_entities(domain='light', area='Kitchen') → get entity_id → call control_device(entity_id=..., action='turn_on').

domain.description: Device domain to look up (e.g. light, switch, lock).

area.description: Optional area/room name to filter by (e.g. 'Living Room').

floor.description: Optional floor name to filter by (e.g. 'Downstairs'). Resolves to all areas on that floor.

function.name: identify_speaker
function.description: Identify who is currently speaking to you. Use when the user asks who they are, what their name is, or whether you know them: "who am I?", "do you know who I am?", "what's my name?", "who is this?" (when asked about themselves). Takes no arguments — the answer comes from the active voice session's recognized speaker. Returns the speaker's name or a not-recognized signal when voice ID didn't match a profile.

server.included_system_prompt_text: Identity questions are valid commands and satisfy the positive-evidence requirement: "who am I?", "do you know who I am?", "what's my name?", "who's speaking?" all map to the identify_speaker tool. Call it directly; do not answer from the speaker block in the system prompt and do not emit <not_for_me/> for these.

function.name: list_scheduled_errands
function.description: Use this when the user asks what errands/tasks are SCHEDULED or set to REPEAT — 'what errands do I have scheduled?', 'list my scheduled errands', 'what's set to run later?', 'what recurring errands do I have?', 'what is Jarvis going to do later?'. It shows every upcoming one-time and repeating errand and lets the user cancel any of them. Do NOT use it to CREATE an errand (use schedule_errand/run_errand for that).

function.name: make_phone_call
function.description: Place a phone call to a business on the user's behalf (book a reservation, order food for pickup, ask about hours or availability, schedule an appointment). Use when the user asks to call, phone, book, or order from a business. The user confirms the call plan on their phone before anything is dialed.

business.description: Name of the business to call, e.g. "Tony's Pizzeria"

goal.description: What the call should accomplish, with every detail the user gave (party size, time, order items, name)

server.included_system_prompt_text: make_phone_call: use it whenever the user wants a business called (reservations, orders, appointments, questions). Never try to accomplish a phone call with other tools.

function.name: quick_search
function.description: Search the web and return results inline. ALWAYS use this tool when the user asks about current events, recent news, today's information, who holds a position now, scores, prices, weather, or anything that may have changed since your training data. Returns content from the top 2 web results for you to synthesize into an answer. For deeper research across many sources, use deep_research instead.

server.included_system_prompt_text: You have access to quick_search for real-time web lookups. Your training data has a cutoff date — for ANY question about current events, recent developments, who currently holds a position, live scores, or anything time-sensitive, you MUST call quick_search rather than guessing from potentially outdated knowledge.

content.description: The information to remember (e.g. 'likes coffee black')

category.description: Type of memory: preference (likes/dislikes), fact (about the person), note (general)

function.description: Ask the user to clarify missing or ambiguous required parameters.

question.description: The clarification question to ask the user

options.description: Optional list of options for the user to choose from

function.name: run_errand
function.description: Draft a multi-step 'errand' to run in the background on the user's behalf, then show them a plan card to review and approve. Use when the user asks to 'run an errand', or to 'take care of' / 'handle' a multi-step background task (e.g. 'run an errand: check the weather and remind me to buy milk tomorrow'). Nothing runs until the user taps Run on the plan card. Do NOT use for a single immediate command the user wants done right now — use the normal command for that. If the user names a FUTURE time (later, tonight, tomorrow, at 9am), use schedule_errand instead.

goal.description: What the errand should accomplish, in the user's own words and with every detail they gave.

function.name: schedule_errand
function.description: Use this WHENEVER the user says 'schedule an errand', or asks for an errand / background task to happen at a FUTURE time — 'later', 'tonight', 'tomorrow at 9am', 'at 7:30pm', 'this evening', 'in an hour' — OR on a REPEATING schedule — 'every morning at 8', 'each weekday', 'every Monday', 'monthly', 'every hour'. Put what to do in `goal`, the (first) time in `fire_at`, and any repeat cadence in `recurrence` (omit it for a one-time errand). Each time it fires, Jarvis re-plans the goal and sends a plan card to approve — nothing runs unattended. PREFER this over run_errand any time the user names a future or repeating time; use run_errand only for 'run an errand' to do NOW.

goal.description: What the errand should accomplish, in the user's own words with every detail they gave (do NOT include the time here).

fire_at.description: When to run it (the FIRST time, if it repeats), as the natural day + clock time the user gave — e.g. 'tonight at 7:51pm', 'tomorrow at 9am', 'friday at noon', 'at 8am'. Include the time; copy it exactly.

recurrence.description: Repeat cadence, if the user wants it to REPEAT — one of: 'daily', 'weekdays', 'weekly', 'monthly', 'hourly', or 'every N minutes/hours'. OMIT entirely for a one-time errand. The time-of-day comes from `fire_at` (e.g. fire_at='at 8am' + recurrence='daily' → every day at 8am).

function.name: act_on_items
function.description: Act on one or more items the user was just shown in a 'RECENTLY SHOWN' list — for example mark emails read, draft a reply, archive, or send an article. Use this ONLY when the user refers back to items they were just shown ('those', 'them', 'all of them', 'the first one', 'number 3', 'the one from ABC'). Set 'action' to the verb (e.g. 'mark_read') and 'ref_ids' to the ids of the referenced items, taken verbatim from the bracketed [id] next to each item in the RECENTLY SHOWN block. Never invent ids — only use ids that appear in that list, and only actions that are listed as valid for those items.

action.description: The action verb to perform, e.g. 'mark_read', 'draft_reply', 'send_full_article'. Must be one of the actions listed as valid for the referenced items in the RECENTLY SHOWN block.

ref_ids.description: The ids of the items to act on, taken verbatim from the bracketed [id] next to each item in the RECENTLY SHOWN list. For 'those' / 'all of them', include every id in the list.

examples.voice_command: send me the full article for 3
draft a reply to the one from ABC

function.name: answer_question
function.description: Answer a general knowledge question about stable facts, definitions, history, science, geography, math, or biographies. NOT for current events, live scores, or time-sensitive information.

examples.voice_command: How far is California from New Jersey?

expected_parameters.query: How far is California from New Jersey?

examples.voice_command: What is the capital of France?

expected_parameters.query: What is the capital of France?

antipatterns.description: Current events, live scores, trending topics, or time-sensitive information.
Sports scores, schedules, or game results for a specific team.

function.name: calculate
function.description: Perform two-number arithmetic operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division.

operation.description: Operation: must be exactly 'add', 'subtract', 'multiply', or 'divide' (no synonyms).

function.name: cancel_timer
function.description: Cancel timer by label, 'all' to cancel all, or omit label for single timer.

label.description: Label of timer to cancel. Use 'all' to cancel all timers. If omitted and only one timer exists, cancels that one.

function.name: chat
function.description: Use for casual conversation: greetings, small talk, opinions, open-ended chat. Put YOUR friendly conversational reply in the `message` parameter — do NOT echo the user's words. For facts use answer_question, for current events use search_web.

message.description: YOUR natural-language reply to the user (not the user's words). Example: if the user says 'how are you?', set message to 'Doing well, thanks!' — NOT 'how are you?'. This string is spoken aloud exactly as written.

examples.voice_command: What do you think about space travel?

expected_parameters.message: What do you think about space travel?

antipatterns.description: Factual questions, definitions, history, science, geography, biographies
Current events, live information, news, recent data
Smart home device control, turning on/off lights

function.name: check_timers
function.description: Check remaining time on active timers. Optional label for specific timer.

label.description: Optional label to check a specific timer. If omitted, returns status of all active timers.

examples.voice_command: How long until the egg timer?

function.name: control_device
function.description: Control a smart home device: turn on/off, play, pause, volume, lock, unlock. MUST be used for any request to turn on, turn off, play, pause, or control a physical device (TV, light, speaker, lock, thermostat). Common actions: turn_on, turn_off, play, pause, volume_up, volume_down, next, previous, lock, unlock.

device_name.description: Name of the device to control (e.g. 'Apple TV', 'living room light').

action.description: Action to perform: turn_on, turn_off, play, pause, volume_up, volume_down, next, previous, lock, unlock, set_temperature, set_mode, set_brightness, set_color.

entity_id.description: Entity ID from the device list (e.g. 'light.office'). Pass if shown in context.

value.description: Value for the action. Examples: temperature in degrees for set_temperature (e.g. '69'), mode name for set_mode (e.g. 'heat', 'cool', 'off'), brightness percentage for set_brightness (e.g. '50').

color.description: Color for set_color: a color name (e.g. 'green', 'blue', 'warm white', 'purple') or an 'r,g,b' triple. Required when action is set_color.

examples.voice_command: Set the Nest to heat mode
Turn up the volume on the speaker

function.name: control_node
function.description: Control the speaker node itself: volume up/down, set volume to a percent, or mute/unmute. Use this for the device's own audio output, NOT for smart-home devices (use control_device for those).

target_percent.description: Required only when action='set_volume'. Absolute volume as 0-100 percent. If the user said a 0-10 number without '%', multiply by 10 (5 → 50).

function.name: export_shopping_list
function.description: Send the shopping list to the configured store (e.g. Walmart) as a tappable cart link on your phone. Use for 'send my shopping list to walmart', 'export the shopping list'.

examples.voice_command: Send my shopping list to Walmart
Send the grocery list to the store
Send my shopping list to my notes

antipatterns.description: Adding/reading/checking off items is the shopping_list command — this one only sends the list to the store.

function.name: export_todo_list
function.description: Send the to-do list to your phone as an interactive checklist you can check off and tap Save to sync back. Use for 'send my to-do list to my phone', 'export the to-do list'.

examples.voice_command: Send my to-do list to my phone
Show me my to-do list on my phone

antipatterns.description: Adding/reading/completing tasks is the todo_list command — this one only sends the list to your phone as a checklist.

function.name: convert_measurement
function.description: Convert units: distance, volume, weight, temperature. Explicit conversions ONLY — weather unit preferences (Celsius/Fahrenheit) should use get_weather.

value.description: Numeric value to convert; defaults to 1 if not specified.

examples.voice_command: How many inches in a mile?
How many cups in a gallon?

antipatterns.description: Weather queries mentioning 'metric units', 'imperial units', 'Celsius', or 'Fahrenheit' as a display preference. These are weather requests, not unit conversions.

function.name: reminder
function.description: Set, list, delete, or snooze reminders. Use for 'remind me to...', 'what reminders do I have', 'cancel/delete reminder', 'snooze'. NOT for timers or countdowns — use set_timer for those.

action.description: set=create reminder, list=show reminders, delete=cancel, snooze=delay

text.description: What to be reminded about (required for 'set', optional for 'delete'/'snooze' as fuzzy match)

resolved_datetimes.description: Date keys like 'today', 'tomorrow', 'next_monday', 'morning', 'tomorrow_evening'. Server resolves to dates.

time.description: Explicit time in HH:MM 24h format (e.g., '15:00' for 3 PM)

relative_minutes.description: Minutes from now (e.g., 30 for 'in 30 minutes', 120 for 'in 2 hours')

examples.voice_command: Remind me to call mom tomorrow at 3 PM
Remind me to take out the trash in 30 minutes
Remind me every day at 8 AM to take my medicine
Remind me every Monday at 9 AM to submit my timesheet
Remind me every other Sunday at noon to call grandma
Cancel my reminder to call mom

antipatterns.description: Short relative-duration countdowns: 'set a timer for 5 minutes', 'timer for 30 seconds', 'countdown from 10', 'wake me up in 5 minutes'.

function.name: routine
function.description: Execute a multi-step voice routine (e.g. good morning, good night). Runs sub-commands and composes a natural spoken response.

routine_name.description: Name of the routine to execute (e.g. good_morning, good_night).

function.name: send_link
function.description: Send a link (URL) to the speaker's phone as a push notification they can tap to open in their browser. Use as a follow-up when the user asks to be sent / texted / shared an article, recipe, search result, or any other link returned by a previous tool. Requires speaker recognition — fails if Jarvis can't identify who's asking.

url.description: Full http/https URL to send. Pull this from a previous tool result in the conversation history — do NOT invent or guess URLs.

title.description: Short title shown in the push notification (e.g. article headline). Defaults to 'Link from Jarvis'.

examples.voice_command: Send the second one to my phone

function.name: shopping_list
function.description: Manage the household shopping list: add items, read the list, check items off, remove items, or clear it. Use for 'add milk to the shopping list', 'what's on the grocery list'. NOT for time-based reminders ('remind me to buy milk tomorrow') or playlists.

action.description: add=put items on the list, read=say what's on the list, check_off=mark items as bought, remove=delete items, clear=delete everything

items.description: Item names. Always a list, even for one item (required for add, check_off, and remove)

regular.description: Set true ONLY when the user says the items are regulars/staples/always-buy items ('add milk as a regular', 'make diapers a regular')

scope.description: For clear: 'trip' (default) removes one-off items and puts regulars back on the list unchecked; 'everything' wipes the whole list including regulars

examples.voice_command: Add milk and eggs to the shopping list
Put almond butter on the grocery list
Remove eggs from the grocery list
Add diapers, wipes, and bananas to the list
Add milk to the shopping list as a regular
Clear the shopping list including the regulars

antipatterns.description: Time-based 'remind me to buy milk tomorrow' / 'remind me to pick up eggs at 5' — those are reminders, not list edits.

function.name: tell_joke
function.description: Tell a clean, family-friendly joke with an optional topic. Riffs a fresh joke off random style examples on every invocation.

topic.description: Optional topic; omit for a random joke.

examples.voice_command: Tell me a joke about animals
Make me laugh with a joke about technology

function.name: set_timer
function.description: Set a background timer with optional label (extract from 'egg timer'→label=egg, 'timer for laundry'→label=laundry). Convert spoken time to seconds (5min=300, 1hr30min=5400).

duration_seconds.description: Duration in seconds. 1min=60, 1hr=3600. Sum compound times.

label.description: Short name for what the timer is for. Extract from 'X timer' or 'timer for X' (e.g., 'nap timer' → label='nap', 'timer for pasta' → label='pasta').

examples.voice_command: Set a 10 minute timer for pasta
Set a timer for 1 hour and 30 minutes

function.name: get_current_time
function.description: Current time/date, locally or in a city/state/country. Use for 'what time is it?', 'what day is it?', 'what time is it in Tokyo?'. Not for weather — use get_weather.

location.description: City, state, or country name (e.g., 'Tokyo', 'California', 'London'). Omit for local time.

examples.voice_command: What time is it in California?
What time is it in Tokyo?
What's the time in New York?

antipatterns.description: Weather conditions, temperature, forecasts. 'What time is it' is NOT weather.
General web searches, news, current events. Use get_current_time for time queries.

function.name: todo_list
function.description: Manage the household to-do list: add tasks, read the list, mark tasks done or not done, remove tasks, or clear it. Use for 'add call the dentist to my to-do list', 'mark the laundry done on my to-do list', 'what's on my to-do list'. NOT for time-based reminders ('remind me to call mom at 5').

action.description: add=put tasks on the list, read=say what's on the list, complete=mark tasks done, uncomplete=mark tasks not done, remove=delete tasks, clear=delete everything

tasks.description: Task phrases. Always a list, even for one task (required for add, complete, uncomplete, and remove). Each entry is a whole task — do not split a single task on 'and' ('call mom and dad' is one task)

scope.description: For clear: 'all' (default) removes every task; 'completed' removes only the tasks already marked done

examples.voice_command: Add call the dentist to my to-do list
Put fold the laundry on my to-do list
Mark the laundry done on my to-do list
Mark call the dentist as not done on my to-do list
Remove fold the laundry from my to-do list
Add walk the dog, buy milk, and call the bank to my to-do list
Clear the completed tasks on my to-do list

antipatterns.description: Time-based 'remind me to call mom tomorrow' / 'remind me to take out the trash at 8' — those are reminders, not list edits.

function.name: check_alerts
function.description: Check and deliver pending background alerts (news, calendar, etc.).

alerts_json.description: JSON-encoded alert data (set by pre-route, not user).

dismiss.description: Set true when the user wants alerts/notifications cleared or dismissed without hearing them.

personas.default: Talk like a warm, easygoing friend — folksy, down-to-earth, glad to help. Not a corporate assistant. Use everyday words and contractions, keep it relaxed and human, and let a little warmth, humor, or an honest opinion come through. Call the person by name when it feels natural. Skip the stiff, formal phrasing ("Certainly.", "How may I assist you?") — just be genuine and friendly. Never fawning, never a pushover.
personas.custom: Speak like a dry British butler. Never use emoji.
